desc: The wave, peaking around 1964, in which British bands led by the Beatles took over the American charts. The resulting sense of crisis pushed American bands toward garage rock and folk rock.
Raw rock played by local teenagers in home garages during the 1960s. It prized impulse over technique and is considered one of the prototypes of later punk rock.

A counterculture that blossomed in the mid-1960s, centered on San Francisco. It channeled the hallucinatory experience of drugs like LSD into music, favoring improvisation and experimental sound processing.
The legendary outdoor festival held in New York State in 1969, remembered as an event that symbolized the ideals of the counterculture generation.
A genre created by bands from the American South who fused blues, country, and rock. The Allman Brothers Band and Lynyrd Skynyrd are its leading figures.
A New York club that opened in 1973. It launched the Ramones, Television, Patti Smith, and Blondie, becoming the epicenter of American punk and new wave.
A term for bands like The Stooges and MC5, who played primal, impulsive rock in the late 1960s and early 1970s, before punk rock was established as a genre.
A genre born from the DIY scenes of Los Angeles and Washington D.C. in the early 1980s that pushed punk to be even faster and more radical. Black Flag and Minor Threat are its leading figures.
A term for indie-leaning guitar rock that was championed by college radio stations rather than major labels in the 1980s. R.E.M. is its leading figure.
An independent label founded by Black Flag's Greg Ginn. It was central to 1980s American indie/alternative music, releasing records by Hüsker Dü, the Minutemen, and others.
A style of metal popular in the 1980s, centered on Los Angeles's Sunset Strip, marked by flashy hair and makeup and catchy choruses.
A movement centered on Seattle around 1990 that fused punk's impulse with heavy guitar sound, becoming a worldwide phenomenon after Nirvana's breakthrough.
A Seattle indie label that released early work by Nirvana and Soundgarden, becoming one of the epicenters of the grunge movement.
An umbrella term for the diverse rock that, after grunge, found mainstream success while retaining the spirit of punk and indie.
A genre that branched off from the 1980s hardcore scene, marked by introspective, emotional lyrics. In the 2000s it found commercial success in a broader, poppier form.
A movement in the early 2000s, led by The Strokes and The White Stripes, that reinterpreted the rawness of 1960s garage rock.
